Quick technical note on subprocessors and export control scope — sending a short summary for the legal record: 

- Services that process medical images: ingestion service (ingest-gateway), temporary storage (s3-like object stores in eu-west-1), GPU inference workers (inference-pool-gpu-eu), and the telemetry pipeline (metrics-relay).
- Which are managed by Redwood vs third parties: GPU workers are Redwood-managed; object storage is customer-configurable but for MedSys will be our eu tenant; we do use a third-party CDN for optimization but it does not persist raw images.
- Export control risk: we do not currently export raw imaging data outside the EU for processing for MedSys; inference artifacts (model weights) are stored in our internal artifact repo (no export). If MedSys requests cross-border processing we will need an extra controls addendum.

Suggested paragraph for TIA / evidence: "Redwood confirms that for the MedSys deployment, all raw medical imaging processing and retention will occur within eu-west-1. Subprocessors that receive access to data are limited to operational staff and processor services listed in the attached subprocessor registry. Redwood does not transfer raw imaging artifacts outside the EEA under the current configuration."

If legal wants different wording, tell me and I’ll iterate.

-Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Runtime
